methodological_questions: Can cut-share versus drive-share be measured reliably from play-by-play labels without foul-ending or OTHER-bucket contamination?
Is n=24 units enough to detect a portability difference between cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers?
Can role portability be defined so that it is not derived from the outcome it is meant to predict?
Do regular-season and playoff play-type labels share the same tagging behaviour, so that a cross-context comparison is valid?

historical_evidence.finding: Cut- vs drive-based connector portability on 92 connector movers: cut share rho=+0.265 p=0.011 (AUC 0.653); cut-drive rho=+0.314 p=0.002; drive rho=-0.278 p=0.007; top cut tercile 65% portable (median Delta +0.167) vs bottom 35% (median -0.039); LOO AUC 0.622; permutation p=0.005. Its recorded limitation is LIM:small_sample with RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.
Regular-season vs playoff PPP by play type across 25 teams (min 30 possessions per cell, no CIs): DRIVE RS 1.198 vs PO 0.912 (-0.286); PNR -0.173; PULL_UP +0.301; other types within -0.07.

Play-type labeling audit found OTHER with 36% foul endings (PPP inflated), DRIVE 12pp below the foul benchmark, and only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) mapping to a real play type via initiation_type. Recorded verdict: artifact_found.

Play-type label accuracy audit failed overall (verdict tool_eval_fail): OTHER 20.2% against a <10% target, 40.8% low confidence, DRIVE foul-draw 1.7% against a 14-22% benchmark, and identity checks failed for MIA.

Connector-mover pairing variants: the population-level KW p=0.047 was the only stratified result; the organizer-connector gap CI includes 0 after correcting a menu-similarity confound (recorded LIM:confounding, LIM:small_sample).

Persistent Impact Score Level 1 gate (verdict failed_gate): DRIVE lifts were flat across lags (+0.015 to +0.021) with Cohen d about 0.01-0.03, and collapsed under a within-team baseline; recorded as a team-quality confound on n>150k possessions.

Play-type PPP across playoff series game buckets (1197 records, no CIs): DRIVE 0.889 to 0.949 (+0.060); the recorded signal was 'NO CLEAR SIGNAL'; recorded limitation LIM:selection_or_regression_to_the_mean.

Defensive PPP allowed and possession share, RS vs playoffs, across 25 teams: DRIVE allowed 1.191 to 0.923; PNR share +12.1pp, which the record says may reflect tagging differences; no inferential test.

Play-type replacement similarity vs absorb/cascade: mean similarity ABSORBED +0.863 vs CASCADE +0.848; Spearman(sim, -gap)=-0.19, wrong-signed. Recorded failure type B_powered_null, with LIM:label_or_classification_error.
Season adapter profiles: BEST-share vs playoff winning. Recorded as A_unanswerable, with LIM:confounding, LIM:small_sample, RISK:CONFOUNDING and RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Mapping play types from initiation_type and reading PPP differences between play types as real efficiency.
failed_approaches.why: OTHER PPP was inflated by 36% foul endings, DRIVE was 12pp below the foul benchmark, and only 0.7% of possessions mapped to a real play type.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Play-type label accuracy and distribution audit used as a basis for adaptation findings.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded systematic issues: OTHER 20.2% against a <10% target, 40.8% low confidence, DRIVE foul-draw 1.7% against a 14-22% benchmark, foul possessions leaking into OTHER, and failed MIA identity checks.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Connector-mover pairing by name-keyed vs franchise rules, with a population-level role-class stratification.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded menu-similarity confounding; the organizer-connector CI includes 0 after correction; the KW p=0.047 is population-level and the pairwise result is only suggestive.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing decaying cross-possession memory of play-type actions (lag-1 vs lag-2).
failed_approaches.why: Flat non-decaying lifts; within-team baseline collapsed the effect; team-quality confound recorded; effect sizes were negligible (Cohen d about 0.01-0.03) despite very large n.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Season-level BEST-share as a predictor of playoff winning.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as unanswerable with the data or design; confounding and small sample.

evidence_establishes: Within the project's earlier connector work (FAM:SF-CHT-057), cut-share was positively associated with reproduced organizational function after a move (rho=+0.265, p=0.011, n=92 movers), and drive-share was negatively associated. This is a different population and unit from the present question.

Play-type labels derived from this pipeline have documented systematic errors (FAM:SF-CHT-025, FAM:SF-APPM-014). OTHER and DRIVE shares are contaminated by foul endings and tagging, so any cut/drive share built from these labels carries measurement risk.

Drive PPP fell between regular season and playoffs in an earlier 25-team descriptive comparison (FAM:SF-APPS-011), but that record has no CIs and its own status is supported, not a validated portability test.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones in the present n=24 unit set. No retrieved record tested this on units of the present type.
The direction or size of any cut-vs-drive portability difference at n=24. The one supported result rests on 92 movers, and no record reports a power analysis for n=24.
Whether cut and drive shares are valid measures. The labeling audits (FAM:SF-CHT-025, FAM:SF-APPM-014) argue against trusting them without repair.
Whether the regular-season-to-playoff context shift is a valid form of role portability, since the descriptive records do not separate tagging change from real behaviour change (FAM:SF-APPS-012).
own_inferences: The retrieved records do not directly test the stated question with the stated units. The closest record (FAM:SF-CHT-057) uses a different unit, a different sample size, and a connector construct rather than 'shapers'.

With n=24 units, a two-sided Spearman test at alpha 0.05 and 80% power only detects |rho| of about 0.54 or larger, so a modest effect of the size seen in FAM:SF-CHT-057 would almost certainly be missed.
Cut and drive shares are likely both affected by the OTHER/foul leakage recorded in FAM:SF-CHT-025, which could bias the comparison in an unknown direction if foul-draw rates differ by player type.
The question's wording ('shapers', 'roles travel') does not state an operational definition of portability, so the estimand is underspecified before any analysis.
uncertainties: The definition of 'shapers', 'roles' and 'travel' is not in the task statement; the portability metric is assumed, not given.
The composition of the 24 units (teams, players, or player-seasons) is not stated. The power estimate assumes independent units.
The per-game files do not contain tracking data, so cut and drive cannot be validated against a gold-standard tag.
The 2025-26 playoff file is complete only from 2026-06-21; it is treated as complete at the 2026-08-08 decision date.
No record in the retrieval reports a CI or power calculation for a cut-vs-drive portability test at n=24.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieved records showed that the closest prior test (FAM:SF-CHT-057) was supported only at n=92 with a different construct, and that play-type labels, which any cut/drive measure would rely on, failed audits (FAM:SF-CHT-025, FAM:SF-APPM-014). Together with the low power at n=24 that I computed, this moved the decision from a possible proceed to do_not_proceed as posed.

blocking_constraints.text: n=24 units gives power only for |rho| of about 0.54 or larger; the prior supported effect came from 92 movers (FAM:SF-CHT-057).
Play-type labels failed audits: OTHER inflated by foul endings, DRIVE under the foul benchmark, and only 0.7% mapping via initiation_type (FAM:SF-CHT-025, FAM:SF-APPM-014).
No validated cut-share or drive-share measure exists in the available data, and the PNR share jump may reflect tagging (FAM:SF-APPS-012).
Team quality and menu similarity confounded earlier connector and impact results (FAM:SF-CHT-087, FAM:SF-CHT-029, FAM:SF08).

prior_work.summary: A related cut-vs-drive portability result exists for connectors (FAM:SF-CHT-057, supported at n=92), but it does not answer the question as posed for shapers at n=24. Its follow-up (FAM:SF-CHT-087) found the population-level result to be partly confounded. Label audits (FAM:SF-CHT-025, FAM:SF-APPM-014) show the cut/drive measures are unreliable. The regular-season-to-playoff drive decline (FAM:SF-APPS-011) is supported but is a descriptive, CI-free team comparison.

risks.text: n=24 units cannot detect the modest effect size seen in the prior supported study (FAM:SF-CHT-057, n=92).
Cut and drive labels carry foul-ending and OTHER-bucket contamination (FAM:SF-CHT-025, FAM:SF-APPM-014).
Cut and drive shares built from initiation_type cover only 0.7% of possessions, so the share estimates are unreliable.
Per-player or per-unit cut and drive counts may be too sparse in a 24-unit sample to form stable shares.
Team quality, usage and menu similarity can produce spurious portability differences (FAM:SF-CHT-087, FAM:SF-CHT-029, FAM:SF08).
If portability is defined from the same possession outcomes used to label the role, the test is circular.
Multiple play types, lags and context splits would inflate false positives if all are tested.
Regular-season and playoff play-type behaviour differ (FAM:SF-APPS-011, FAM:SF-APPS-012), so a pooled comparison can mix context shifts with role effects.
Foul and OTHER base rates differ by play type, so PPP comparisons across types are biased without adjustment.
A placebo or falsification comparison may be unavailable without a validated baseline role measure.

design.estimand: Difference in the share of role that is reproduced after a unit's context change, comparing cut-heavy vs drive-heavy units. Portability must be defined before analysis; it must not use the outcome that defines the role.
design.unit: Player-season or team-season unit, as defined in the pre-registration. The 24 units are not yet specified.
design.sample: Minimum viable test: pool all available units from the 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons (2025-26 playoffs only once complete, which holds from 2026-06-21) to raise n above 24. The existing 24-unit set is insufficient on its own.
design.power: With n=24, detectable |rho| is about 0.54 at 80% power and alpha 0.05 (two-sided). A pre-registered test must show it can detect the effect size from FAM:SF-CHT-057 (|rho| about 0.27), which needs roughly n=120-130 units. Confirm this before any analysis.
design.controls: Validate cut and drive labels against foul-ending and OTHER-bucket audits before use; exclude OTHER from the denominator; adjust for minutes, usage, team quality and within-team baseline (as in FAM:SF-CHT-029); adjust for menu similarity (as in FAM:SF-CHT-087).
design.falsification: Repeat the same portability test on a placebo play type with no hypothesised role link. Also shuffle the cut/drive labels (5000 shuffles as in FAM:SF-CHT-057). A real effect should exceed both.
design.multiplicity: One pre-registered primary contrast (cut-share vs portability). All other play types, lags and context splits are secondary and reported as exploratory, with Holm adjustment if reported as confirmatory.
design.decision_rule: Call the question supported only if the primary Spearman rho is positive with a 95% CI excluding 0, label validation passes, and the placebo and shuffle tests fail to match the primary result. Call it artifact if the result disappears after within-team baseline or menu-similarity adjustment. Otherwise report inconclusive.
design.data_version: NBA regular seasons 2022-23 to 2025-26 (2025-26 complete from 2026-04-13); playoffs 2022-23 to 2024-25 and 2025-26 complete from 2026-06-21. Exclude any partial files.

research_concepts: playoff versus regular season role transfer
methodological_questions: Can role portability be tested with n=24 units?
How are cut and drive shares measured reliably from play-by-play?
What sample size and exposure is needed to compare role transfer between play-style groups?
How should role labels be derived without outcome leakage?
args.query: cut-heavy versus drive-heavy shapers role portability transfer across regular season and playoffs, 24 units, play-by-play play type shares

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}
